Comment_1: INF-03 ROUTE (A): the least-privilege policy that lets the deploy identity create and use the terraform state backend. PREPARED, NOT ATTACHED -- attaching it is a permission change and belongs to the account owner.
Comment_2: Apply with:  aws iam put-user-policy --user-name github-actions --policy-name VyomQuantTerraformStateBackend --policy-document file://infra/iam/terraform-state-backend-policy.json   then:  python scripts/bootstrap_terraform_state.py --apply
Comment_3: SCOPED TO TWO NAMED RESOURCES. s3:CreateBucket cannot be scoped to a bucket that does not exist yet in the usual sense, so it is granted on the exact ARN of the bucket terraform/backend.tf expects and no other. Measured denials this replaces: s3:CreateBucket ('no identity-based policy allows'), dynamodb:DescribeTable, dynamodb:ListTables.
Comment_4: DELIBERATELY ABSENT: s3:DeleteBucket, s3:DeleteObjectVersion and dynamodb:DeleteTable. Terraform never needs to destroy its own backend, and a state backend that the deploy identity can delete is a backend one bad command can lose. State history is the thing that makes a bad apply recoverable.
